jsonObj.suggestedValue: Chhath Puja is the most significant festival in Bihar and the Mithila region, dedicated to Surya Dev (the Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya. In Bandwar, the festival is celebrated at the [[bandh|bandh]] along the [[burhi-gandak|Burhi Gandak]], with the entire village gathering on the riverbank. A large idol of Surya Dev, mounted on his chariot with seven horses, is set up at the bandh, and the village observes four days of rigorous fasting and Vedic ritual.

Chhath Puja is the most important festival of Bihar — more significant, in popular practice, than Diwali or Holi. It is dedicated to Surya Dev (the Sun) and Chhathi Maiya (also known as Usha, his sister/wife), and is observed over four days with strict fasting and Vedic ritual. The festival has no priestly intermediary — devotees pray directly to the sun. In Bandwar, the festival is celebrated at the [[bandh|bandh]] along the [[burhi-gandak|Burhi Gandak]], and it is the single largest gathering of the village in the course of the year.
